crumbs.name: Knowledge Based Professions and their Future

children.name: Harmonising Privacy Frameworks
children.blurb: Harmonising privacy frameworks in AI practice means aligning obligations across the major data protection regimes, including the GDPR, the UK GDPR, California's CPRA, Brazil's LGPD and China's PIPL, so that a single processing activity can be assessed once against a common control set.

children.name: Incident Response and Breach Notification
children.blurb: Incident response and breach notification in an AI context covers detecting, containing, assessing, and reporting security events that involve personal data or AI systems.

children.name: Cross-Border Data Transfers
children.blurb: Cross-border data transfers in AI work cover the movement of personal data, training data, model outputs, and related metadata from one legal jurisdiction to another.

children.name: AI Supply Chain Liability
children.blurb: AI supply chain liability concerns the allocation of legal responsibility for harm caused by an AI system across the organizations that build, train, integrate, deploy, or use it.

children.name: Biometric and Surveillance Law
children.blurb: Biometric and surveillance law covers the collection, use, retention, and sharing of biometric identifiers such as face, fingerprint, iris, voice, and gait data, along with surveillance technologies like facial recognition, automated license plate readers, and video analytics.

sections.body: This field covers how organizations handle personal data when building or using AI systems, and how they meet legal duties after something goes wrong. Artificial intelligence is now being used to scan privacy policies against multiple legal regimes, to classify data flows for transfer rules, and to draft breach notices under tight time limits. In biometric and surveillance work, AI systems are being deployed to redact faces from video, to check consent records, and to flag high risk processing before it starts. In supply chains, AI tools are being used to map which vendors touch training data or model outputs, and to compare their contract terms against regulatory requirements. The work is operational, not theoretical, and it sits inside law firms, compliance teams, and regulators.
sections.heading: What this covers

sections.body: The field is uneven. Basic breach notification workflows are well supported by software, but the legal judgment about whether a breach is notifiable still rests with people. Cross border transfer rules remain fragmented, and no single AI tool has solved the problem of mapping every national restriction accurately. Biometric law is changing quickly, with many state and local rules, and the site tracks 210 compliance and regulation pages that reflect this spread. AI supply chain liability is the least settled area, because courts have not yet produced a clear line of cases on who is responsible when a model built by one vendor harms a user through another vendor's integration. Honest limits include the fact that automated compliance checks can miss context, and that breach response tools cannot replace a lawyer's duty to report to a regulator.
sections.heading: Where the work stands

sections.body: A reader looking for a single starting point would begin with Harmonising Privacy Frameworks, which explains how different laws overlap and where they conflict. Incident Response and Breach Notification then covers the practical steps after a data loss, including timelines and regulator expectations. Cross-Border Data Transfers moves from domestic rules to the harder question of moving data between countries. AI Supply Chain Liability shifts attention from the data itself to the vendors and model providers in the chain. Biometric and Surveillance Law is the most specific page, dealing with facial recognition, fingerprints, and other sensitive identifiers that privacy frameworks often treat as a special category. Together these pages move from general principles to concrete risk areas, and a reader can follow them in that order or jump to the one that matches an active problem.
